Emiliano Zapata. The Mexican agrarian revolutionary leader whose 1911 Plan de Ayala became the moral centre of the Mexican Revolution. His cry of "Land and Liberty" mobilised southern peasants and campesinos against the Porfiriato's hacienda system.

Zapata led peasant armies in the state of Morelos, fighting for the return of communal lands—the ejidos—that had been stolen during the Porfiriato era. In 1911, he issued the Plan de Ayala, which demanded immediate land redistribution and the dissolution of haciendas. This was far more radical than the reforms proposed by Francisco Madero. His famous slogan "Tierra y Libertad," Land and Liberty, became the rallying cry for agrarian reform across Mexico. Zapata rejected both Madero and later leaders as insufficiently radical, remaining in armed rebellion for a full decade. In 1919, he was assassinated by a political rival under ambiguous circumstances, but his legend grew into that of a legendary martyr of the revolution. His agrarian program directly inspired Article 27 of the 1917 Mexican Constitution, which mandates land reform. Decades later, Lázaro Cárdenas would finally implement the large-scale land redistribution following Zapata's vision, fulfilling the promise that Zapata had died fighting for.
